senses.sense_definition: To officially declare a deceased person to be a saint in Christian tradition.

examples.text: The Catholic Church moved to <w>canonize</w> the beloved nun several decades after her death.
Before the Pope can <w>canonize</w> a candidate, several verified miracles must be documented.

senses.sense_definition: To treat, regard, or revere someone or something as extraordinarily virtuous or heroic.

examples.text: The public began to <w>canonize</w> the political leader, ignoring all of his personal faults.
We should evaluate historical figures fairly rather than simply <w>canonize</w> them without critique.

senses.sense_definition: To accept or establish an artistic, literary, or musical work into the standard repertoire or cultural canon.

examples.text: Literary critics tend to <w>canonize</w> novels that define the anxieties of a particular generation.
Academic institutions helped <w>canonize</w> early cinema as an important art form worthy of study.

senses.sense_definition: To formally authorize and include a religious text as part of the official biblical canon.

examples.text: Early religious councils met to <w>canonize</w> specific scriptures while excluding various others.
Scholars continue to study the historical process used to <w>canonize</w> the books of the Old Testament.

senses.sense_definition: To officially approve, sanction, or authorize an institution, practice, or doctrine.

examples.text: The council sought to <w>canonize</w> the new administrative procedures throughout all regional branches.
By following this standard architecture, later builders would <w>canonize</w> the design for future centuries.
